title: fix(adaptive): a 2D Adaptive takes a start point and an exit point
body:
## What changed

The 2D Adaptive (`Adaptive2D`) takes a start point and an exit point (slice of #1448). The picks are the shared operation-level `picks` field of #3339. The command, the project file, the stamp and MCP `edit_operation` need no change.

- `crates/app/src/operation/pick_kinds.rs`: `Adaptive2D` is now `PickCapability::Region`. Only the Adaptive2D arm changes. The door refusal of the settings that cannot hold a pick is added to `pick_refusal`.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive_picks.rs` (new): the door (`adaptive_pick_refusal`), the picked entry, the piece order, the refusals, and the exit run back on the posted path (`exit_on_path`).
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_hsm.rs`: `choose_entry` uses the start point as the seed. The pieces are ordered by `order_pieces`. A picked plan that falls back to the rings, or that keeps an overload, is refused by name. The budget unit test moves to `pocket_hsm_ring.rs` (the same test, so that the file stays under 400 lines).
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket.rs`: one hook after `emit_pocket_passes` for the exit.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive_avoid.rs`: a pick in a "Do not touch" keep-out is refused with the item names.
- `crates/motion/src/approach.rs`: two runtime fields, `start_point` and `exit_point`. They are not saved. `crates/app/src/operation/adaptive_pick_op.rs` (new) lays the op's picks over the generation copy, or refuses them.
- `crates/app/src/operation/wcs_yaw.rs`: under a Z-rotated work offset the Adaptive picks turn into the generation frame, as the Slot picks do.
- UI: the Lead in / Lead out tab of the 2D Adaptive draws the Start point and Exit point groups (`start_exit_rows::region_groups`, drawn from `op_page.rs` because `mill2d_page.rs` is already over 400 lines). The viewport pick and the marks take the 2D Adaptive.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3327-adaptive-start-exit.md`.

## The law

- Start: the start point is the seed of the HSM plan. The helix (or the plunge) goes down there on each level, through the same entry law and the same triangle room as the automatic seed. The planner then grows the cleared area from that bore and measures each cut on its stock.
- Exit: the last pass of each level ends where the plan ends, on its closing ride along the walls. Then the tool runs back along the same posted moves in reverse (one round of the outer wall at most) to the point nearest the exit point, and climbs out there. A reversed line is the same line and a reversed arc is the same arc, so the run back cuts no new material and makes no feed-feed crossing. The piece nearest the exit point is cut last.
- The cut geometry does not change otherwise. Without a pick no new code runs.

## Refusals (by name, the pick is never moved, nothing is cut)

- `the start point (x, y) is outside the area the tool centre can reach ...`
- `the helix of radius r has no room at the start point (x, y) - the tool centre has c mm of room there and the helix needs n ...` (the plan's own 0.6 helix share)
- `the start|exit point (x, y) is inside the 'Do not touch' keep-out of <names> ...`
- `the exit point (x, y) is d mm from the closing ride of the last pass along the walls - the most is L ...` (L = 1.5 tool diameters + stock to leave, the contour's reach law)
- `the exit point ... is at the piece of the area where the cut starts, and n other piece(s) are cut after it ...`
- `an exit point needs the tool to climb out after the last pass of each level ...` (a level link that stays down)
- `the plan from the start point does not hold the optimal load (<planner note>) ...`
- `the HSM plan <reason> - the Offset rings or the trochoid that would cut the area instead do not take a start or exit point ...`
- At the door and at generation: a tilted (3+2) op, the Trochoidal method, Pass starts at Inside or Outside, a rest pass, and a start point with a Ramp or Arc entry.

## Readings

On a rectangle 60 x 40, tool D10, helix R2 (motion fixture):

- Automatic seed (30, 20): widest cut on the shape-mask meter 1.62 mm. Start point (15, 12): 1.79 mm. The limit in the test is 2.03 mm (the optimal load step with the plan's margin and the grid's).
- Start points (20, 15), (25, 20), (15, 12) are taken. A start point at (40, 25) makes the spiral keep "the least overload": it is refused. A start point at (12, 12) makes the plan cross itself: it is refused with that reason.
- Exit point (58, 20): each level ends at (55, 20). `crossed_pairs` is empty. The first try (a run back on the planner's walk, before the arc fit) read two crossings between the two arc fits, so the run back is made on the posted moves.

## Pinning tests

- `camcraft-motion` `pass_start_levels` (`adaptive_picks` module):
  - `the_start_point_is_where_the_helix_goes_down_on_each_level` (two levels, no overload note, no crossing, widest cut under the limit)
  - `the_exit_point_is_where_the_last_pass_ends_on_each_level` (two levels, no crossing)
  - `a_point_the_plan_cannot_hold_is_refused_by_name`
- `camcraft-app` `start_exit_shared` (`adaptive` module):
  - `the_entry_is_at_the_start_point_and_the_last_pass_ends_at_the_exit_point` (golden CL `adaptive2d_start_exit_picks.cl`)
  - `the_picks_hold_under_a_90_degree_wcs_yaw`
  - `a_point_the_plan_cannot_hold_is_refused_by_name_and_nothing_is_cut` (also the door: tilt, Trochoidal, Pass starts at Inside, Ramp entry)
  - `the_picks_ride_the_command_undo_the_file_and_the_stamp` (undo restores the previous path to the move; no pick plans the earlier path to the move)
  - `mcp_edit_operation_sets_the_adaptive_picks` (`edit_operation`, `get_job` reads them back, `undo` clears them, `list_operation_types` says `start: true, exit: true`)
  - `the_2d_adaptive_takes_a_start_and_an_exit_point`, and `every_kind_has_one_pick_capability_and_only_the_taken_ones_take_a_pick` (updated)
- `camcraft-ui` lib: `the_2d_adaptive_lead_tab_has_both_point_groups_and_takes_an_exit`, `a_2d_adaptive_takes_the_viewport_pick_and_shows_its_marks`

New test files join existing suites (`pass_start_levels/`, `start_exit_shared/`). No new top-level test binary.

## Goldens moved

None. One golden is new: `crates/app/tests/golden/adaptive2d_start_exit_picks.cl`. A path without a pick runs no new code (see the gate: `golden_cl`, the example catalog suites).

## Not exercised

- The keep-out refusal has no pinning fixture. The code is one `contains` test on the keep-out region that `adaptive_spiral_avoid_on` already builds.
- The "climb out" refusal (a level link that stays down) and the "exit at the start's piece" refusal have no fixture.
- A plunge entry at a start point is taken by the door. Its first turn out of a tool-size bore is the planner's existing note, not an overload refusal; no fixture.
- The Trochoidal method stays refused (its seed is on the medial line). #3932 (the trochoidal entry slots to a wall) is a separate path; this PR does not change it.
- No machine run.

## Why `fix`

The issue is labelled `bug` (the 2D Adaptive refused a start and an exit point that #1448 says it takes), and the earlier slice of the same family (#3325, the Slot) shipped as `fix(slot)`. So this PR is a `fix` too, and it merges when it is reviewed.

## Gate

All on the final head `3764e7ed9` (the branch with `origin/main` merged in; one conflict in `start_exit_shared.rs`, where #3981 and this PR each added lines to the gate map and to one assertion; both kept), local Mac, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=8`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 875 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (83.3 min). The plan includes `motion suites: pass_start_levels`, `app suites: start_exit_shared`, `golden_cl`, `ui suites: lib`, and the example catalog suites by name: `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` (all ok).
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (14.5 min).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean on the code head before the merge of main (the merge changed only test lines in `start_exit_shared.rs`).

Note: under load, the quick gate marked `the_start_point_is_where_the_helix_goes_down_on_each_level` slow (>60 s with 8 test threads) in the first run, not in the final run. The test plans one 60 x 40 area on two levels.

Heavy step: none. This is a P2 issue, and AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review" gives a targeted heavy step only to a P1 PR under the safety floor.

Changelog: The 2D Adaptive takes a start point and an exit point: the entry goes down at the start point and the cleared area grows from there, and the last pass of each level runs back along its closing ride to the point nearest the exit point; a point that the plan cannot hold is refused by name.
